title: Farmed American, Dubia, and lobster cockroach (Blattodea) welfare: recommendations and research directions
content:
Abstract
Billions of cockroaches (Blattodea) are farmed each year for food, feed, traditional medicine, and cosmetics. Despite strong evidence consistent with the capacity for sentience (according to some precautionary frameworks) in adult Blattodea, little work has been done to understand what may affect their welfare in farmed contexts. Accordingly, we use the Five Domains framework to assess factors related to nutrition, environment, physical health, and behavior that may affect the mental state, and thereby welfare, in three species of farmed cockroaches: American cockroaches (Periplaneta americana [Linnaeus]), orange-spotted or “Dubia” cockroaches (Blaptica dubia [Serville]), and lobster cockroaches (Nauphoeta cinerea [Olivier]). Accordingly, we begin by reviewing the basic biology of each species. We then survey the available information on rearing, transport, and slaughter for farmed cockroaches. We describe how practices in these three areas may affect their welfare under the Five Domains model, ultimately making recommendations for how cockroach welfare may be improved. Finally, we conclude by highlighting a number of future research directions that would inform our understanding of these animals’ welfare and possible mental states.
